courses: Business & Economy in the Age of AI
New Issues in Contemporary Social Theory

core: Economic theory, market mechanisms and macroeconomic policy
Law, politics and institutions in economic decisions
Welfare, distribution, fairness and ethical policy choices
Mathematical, statistical, programming and empirical economic inquiry
Climate, sustainability and collective economic policy
International, labour, migration and regulatory economic applications
adjacent: Behavioral and social explanation of inequality and public decisions
Environmental impacts, collective action and sustainability governance
questions: How should economic choices be evaluated for welfare, equity and social consequences?
How can economic evidence and institutions inform fair and sustainable public decisions?

trace: Actual AI labour/productivity, market structure, innovation and regulation provide a concrete contemporary economic/institutional application, not a full labour-economics course.
Actual money, banking, financial institutions and policy mechanisms deepen institutional macro/finance analysis.
Actual micro/macro models, markets and incentives establish the economic foundation, not general policy context.
Actual macroeconomic, labour-market and open-economy models analyze growth, inflation, unemployment and fiscal/monetary choices.
Actual consumer/producer choice, uncertainty, market power, factor markets, efficiency and externalities supply economic explanation and research appraisal.
Actual public goods, externalities, taxation/spending, welfare and social-insurance policy integrate economic models with equity and evidence.
Description supports OLS/GLS/IV, inference/Monte Carlo and an empirical paper. No unlisted FE, DiD, matching or RDD training is assumed.
Description supports biases, heuristics, framing and experiments in economic decisions. No absent detailed outline or economic field experiment is invented.
Actual international trade/business, investment, global value chains and governance support cross-border economic institutions; business strategy is not full international-economic theory.

Actual firm, market, value and stakeholder foundations support institutional economic choices and formal banking/trade preparation; climate program uses firm-level cost/impact decisions, not a generic extra gateway.
Actual design, measurement, sampling, R inference and data collection supply empirical foundations and formal preparation.

Actual inclusion/identity safety and supervised ethical survey design, original data, measures and regression provide substantive human-behavior/inequality mechanisms and empirical practice; no invented income-policy dataset.
Actual R data preparation, visualization, text/spatial data and research workflow support empirical economic questions without a guaranteed economics dataset.
Actual calculus, equations and dynamic-model reasoning support mathematical economic analysis; no complete matrix/multivariable sequence inferred.
Actual probability, estimation/testing and Monte Carlo methods provide rigorous statistical foundations for economic evidence.
Actual public goods/externalities, collective action, institutions, stakeholders and policy evaluation/advice provide substantive sustainability governance.
Actual climate drivers, impacts, justice and governance ground the physical/social object of climate policy, not discounting or integrated economic assessment.
Actual life-cycle environmental/social impacts and cost/revenue analysis supply a concrete product/process assessment approach, not macroeconomic carbon-cost modelling.
Actual legal systems, public/private law, rights, social control and legal reasoning supply the legal-institutional foundation and formal preparation; not Dutch fiscal/social doctrine.
Actual constitutional/administrative institutions, rights, participation and procedural fairness illuminate public authority and policy constraints, not social-insurance/tax doctrine.
Actual EU competences, sources, free movement and judicial remedies provide a legal-economic regulatory connection, not Dutch tax/social doctrine.
Actual ethical theories and reasoned evaluation inform normative welfare, fairness and intergenerational policy judgment; not an economic-welfare model substitute.
Actual comparative political systems, institutions and democratic change provide institutional explanation for economic decision contexts.
Actual EU institutional analysis and amendment-coding research connect economic governance questions to observed political decision processes.
Description supports policy-making phases/globalization, a concrete case and policy memos; no guaranteed economic topic or absent detailed outline.
Actual class, race/gender, socialization and institutions provide sociological explanation of distribution and social opportunity without claiming economic inequality metrics.
Actual qualitative design, interviews/interpretation and reflexivity contribute a specific empirical approach to social consequences alongside quantitative economics.
Actual modernity, imperialism, colonial responses and social theory offer historical-social explanation of institutions and stratification; do not replace economic models.
Description-only environmental-justice movement cases, anti-colonialism and degrowth inform distributional and political conflict over sustainability; no causal economic model is inferred.
Actual trust, civil society, solidarity and empirical organizational/social inquiry develop collective and institutional explanations of social well-being.
Actual cognition, social influence, bias and research design provide psychological explanation of public/economic decisions; no assigned economic experiment assumed.

Actual experimental/quasi-experimental design, multivariable analysis, diagnostics and R reports strengthen empirical evaluation. Psychology data and models are not invented econometric identification methods.

candidates.label: Climate, fair sustainability and collective economic decisions

selection.assessment: Closest economic/institutional response passes the confirmed core. Behavioral/inequality then climate-governance candidates each preserve economic/empirical substance while materially changing explanatory objects and methods. All pass qualitative and numerical distinctness; three maximum, no extra career-generated slot.

alternatives.label: Economics, institutions & public policy
alternatives.labelReason: The completed program combines actual economics and empirical foundations with institutional/public-policy study, without claiming a full Leiden degree or named formal route.
alternatives.concept: Combine economic theory and empirical analysis with law, political institutions and public policy. Mathematical/statistical foundations, money/trade and contemporary economic applications support decisions about markets, government and welfare.
progression: Actual mathematical/statistical and law gateways precede formal dependents; BENGATE101 precedes banking/trade in the closest. P2 BENGATE102 precedes leadership survey research. P3 climate foundations precede the only planned 2027h2 life-cycle course; firm foundation comes later and has no formal dependent here. Data science in P2/P3 is later but before econometrics; earlier BENGATE102 supplies R/statistical grounding. Micro/public economics co-occur under real offerings with introductory economics and formal prerequisites complete; advisory concurrency is not a new hard gate.

alternatives.label: Economics, behavior & inequality
alternatives.labelReason: The completed program combines actual economics and empirical foundations with behavioral/social explanation and inequality, without claiming a full Leiden degree or named formal route.
alternatives.concept: Retain economic theory and empirical policy inquiry while examining behavior, social opportunity and inequality through psychology, sociology and original survey research. Normative and institutional analysis connect economic choices to well-being and social consequences.
progression: Actual mathematical/statistical and law gateways precede formal dependents; BENGATE101 precedes banking/trade in the closest. P2 BENGATE102 precedes leadership survey research. P3 climate foundations precede the only planned 2027h2 life-cycle course; firm foundation comes later and has no formal dependent here. Data science in P2/P3 is later but before econometrics; earlier BENGATE102 supplies R/statistical grounding. Micro/public economics co-occur under real offerings with introductory economics and formal prerequisites complete; advisory concurrency is not a new hard gate.
alternatives.distinctness: Compared with the closest, replaces banking/trade/AI and EU-political emphasis with sustained sociological/psychological explanation, original survey work and social opportunity. Five actual changes implement that priority; economics is retained.

alternatives.label: Economics, climate & public decisions
alternatives.labelReason: The completed program combines actual economics and empirical foundations with climate impacts and sustainability governance, without claiming a full Leiden degree or named formal route.
alternatives.concept: Retain economic theory, quantitative evidence and institutions while concentrating on climate impacts, life-cycle assessment, environmental justice and collective sustainability decisions. These approaches complement economic policy analysis; they do not reproduce Leiden’s integrated climate-economic model.
progression: Actual mathematical/statistical and law gateways precede formal dependents; BENGATE101 precedes banking/trade in the closest. P2 BENGATE102 precedes leadership survey research. P3 climate foundations precede the only planned 2027h2 life-cycle course; firm foundation comes later and has no formal dependent here. Data science in P2/P3 is later but before econometrics; earlier BENGATE102 supplies R/statistical grounding. Micro/public economics co-occur under real offerings with introductory economics and formal prerequisites complete; advisory concurrency is not a new hard gate.
alternatives.distinctness: Compared with the closest, four substantive changes replace financial/trade/AI/EU-political emphasis with climate science, life-cycle impacts/costs, environmental justice and sustainability governance. Compared with the behavioral program, different environmental objects and policy-evaluation methods organize the work. No arbitrary threshold repair.

blocks: Both introduce economic reasoning, models and societal applications. Leiden more explicitly integrates normative/institutional perspectives; these are supplied by other UCR courses, not asserted identical.
Both analyze macroeconomic mechanisms, growth, employment and policy. UCR develops international dimensions and its own model sequence.
Both study microeconomic choice, firms/markets, uncertainty and welfare-relevant intervention. The organization and advanced topic weights differ.
Both analyze government intervention, taxation/spending, public goods, efficiency and equity using economic reasoning and evidence.
Both develop regression-based economic inference. UCR includes OLS/GLS/IV and Stata/Monte Carlo; tools and the sequence differ. This is not a claim to all advanced causal-policy methods.
Both study psychologically informed economic decisions. UCR description confirms biases, heuristics, framing and experimental learning; no more detailed unprovided syllabus is assumed.
Both address international economic relations, trade/investment and institutions. UCR uses a business/governance perspective rather than reproducing the full international-economic theory sequence.
Both develop statistical reasoning and empirical analysis. UCR embeds inference in broader research design and actual data collection.
Both teach practical R-oriented data preparation, visualization and programming. Domain examples, assignments and breadth differ.

Both provide mathematical tools for economic modelling and data reasoning. UCR emphasizes calculus and dynamic equations; no exact equivalence of the full economist-specific mathematics sequence is claimed.
Both introduce legal systems, sources and institutions. UCR integrates socio-legal reasoning; it does not supply all economics-specific legal applications.
Both study EU law, institutions and internal-market regulation. Leiden focuses the package on European economic law; UCR offers a broader legal foundation. This does not replace Social Law.
Both examine political institutions and processes relevant to economic decisions. UCR emphasizes comparative politics rather than an economist-specific introduction.
Both examine policy-making and implementation across political contexts. UCR uses a sugar case and policy memos; Leiden develops the economic/bureaucratic interaction explicitly.

notes.text: Only the confirmed first 120 EC are academically compared. The complete published 180-EC outline includes genuine open study and a named required final year, whose detailed content, project assessment/access and full progression remain unassessed. UCR economics and empirical inquiry have real institutional, behavioral or climate connections, with explicit specialist legal, labour/migration, climate-modelling and causal-method gaps. The published 10-EC project is outside the assessed core; optional UCR research is additional and does not replace it.

audience.programmeDescription: Economics & Society at Leiden combines economic theory and empirical analysis with law, politics and institutions. Students examine welfare, inequality, climate change, migration and labour markets, and learn to assess economic policy and its social consequences. The programme is taught in The Hague in cooperation with Erasmus School of Economics. Tutoring supports academic and career development.
audience.comparisonExplanation: This qualified academic-core comparison assesses the confirmed first 120 EC with Package A. Three UCR programs combine economic theory and empirical analysis with institutions, behavior and inequality, or climate governance. All 180 EC of the published outline remain visible, but the final 30 required EC and project are shown only at outline level and are outside the academic comparison. Dutch fiscal/social law, specialist labour/migration study, integrated climate-economic modelling and some causal methods remain differences.

curriculum.limitation: The published outline totals 180 EC, including 30 EC of elective space and a 10-EC bachelor project. Detailed third-year, cohort and project requirements remain unconfirmed. This is an indicative programme outline, not a certified complete degree pathway.

acceptance.claim: The confirmed first120EC economic, empirical and institutional core supports meaningful full UCR programs focused on public institutions, behavior/inequality or climate decisions. All180 published outline EC remain, with genuine open30 and required final30 separately shown; detailed final-year formation/project/access are not academically compared or certified. Known specialist legal, labour/migration, climate-model and causal-method gaps remain.
acceptance.targetContext: Ordinary Leiden Economics & Society BSc50996/1001O8921, dated2026–2027 core with neutral PackageA, no invented formal degree route or future eligibility guarantee.
acceptance.challengeMethod: Separately identified same-AI source-first final pass against actual primary/UCR evidence and exact finished inputs; no independent human/separate agent endorsement.

uncertainties.fact: The full public outline names/weights the final year, but detailed current third-year units, project handbook/entry/assessment and applicable cohort bridge remain unavailable or unconfirmed in the guide.

adverseResolutions.resolution: Required final-year work deepens economic theory, legal-economic doctrine, advanced causal identification or demanding independent research.
adverseResolutions.effectOnClaim: Such study could change full-degree comparability and is outside the assessed core. The current first120EC economic/empirical/institutional substance and actual full UCR programs remain meaningful at the stated limited scope; named credits are preserved without invented detail or equivalence.

adverseResolutions.resolution: The final year emphasizes broader interdisciplinary political economy, historical/contextual study or accessible societal-economic research.
adverseResolutions.effectOnClaim: Do not import hoped-for content or project permission. The same first120EC claim and known specialist gaps remain; neither full project formation nor progression is certified.

uncertainties.fact: Package A/B are alternative annual choices; current formal access/minor/project rules are not established by the historical 2025–2026 OER.

adverseResolutions.resolution: A current regulation or handbook changes future preparation, approval, placement or project conditions.
adverseResolutions.effectOnClaim: No access entitlement, waiver or future offering is claimed. Retain the dated, neutral Package A core and reconcile new material evidence only in authorized follow-up. Historical OER remains historical; public names/weights are not a full eligibility certificate.
